implementation_summary: New pure module ranking.ts. IMPACT_EFFORT_BY_RULE gives a default for every BE-305 rule (missing/duplicate title and description, duplicate-content, no-h1, multiple-h1, skipped-heading-level, missing-alt, broken-link), for unlinked-page and for all ten MARKETING_SIGNALS keys. The marketing part is typed as Record<MarketingSignalKey, ...>, so the type check fails if a signal has no entry. IMPACT_EFFORT_BY_SEVERITY maps the tool's severities (Blocker/Major high, Minor medium, Suggestion low) and axe's impact names (critical/serious high, moderate medium). Lookup is case-insensitive and ignores prototype keys such as 'constructor'. DEFAULT_IMPACT_EFFORT is medium/medium. Lookup order is rule, then severity, then default. scoreFindings fills only impact or effort that is undefined or null, returns new objects and never changes a set value. rankFindings sorts by impact (high first), then lower effort, then urlPath (plain code-unit compare, the same in every locale), then Section order ('s1' < 's2' < 's10'; whole-page null first), then rule, target and the old id. It renumbers AF-001… in ranked order using formatFindingId, scores any unset values first and throws TypeError when a value is not on the scale. rankFindingsWithIdMap also returns old id -> new id, with an optional start number. checkCitations(findings, pages) reports 'unknown-page' (urlPath, or any entry in pages[]), 'unknown-section' and 'missing-section' (null sectionId on a rule not in WHOLE_PAGE_RULES). WHOLE_PAGE_RULES lists the title, description and heading-outline rules. pages accepts AuditPage or PageContent shape ({urlPath, sections:[{id}]}).

risks: Renumbering: rankFindings gives new AF ids in ranked order, so ids already cited elsewhere (SeoBasics.findingIds, AccessibilityBasics.findingIds, PhoneLayout.findingIds, marketing evidence, assessment evidence, recommendation findingIds) go stale unless remapped. BE-192 should use rankFindingsWithIdMap and remap them, or rank before anything cites ids. The BE-192 plan text says 'keeping AF ids', which conflicts with this task's 'assigns ids AF-001… in ranked order'; I followed this task.

Citation strictness: per the spec, null sectionId is allowed only for title, description and heading-outline rules. accessibility-basics.ts (BE-307) emits checker findings with sectionId null, and duplicate-content may also be cited with null, so checkCitations will flag those as 'missing-section' until their producers cite a Section or WHOLE_PAGE_RULES is widened by a planned change.
Default impact and effort values are product judgement (Q-14). A reviewer should confirm the table, e.g. duplicate-content medium/high and ctas/lead-forms high/medium.
FindingSeverity in @qa/types is Blocker/Major/Minor/Suggestion. The axe names critical/serious/moderate are mapped too, but no current producer stores them in severity.
